source_document.body:
2026 SEMA Show • This Batmobile-Looking Lamborghini Temerario Is on Display at SEMA
BYD's YANGWANG U9 Xtreme Sets New Production Car Top Speed Record With 312.65 MPH (503.17 KPH) Run
7 photos
Photo: BYD
Following a spectacular crash at more than 224 mph (360 kph), BYD's $3 million electric hypercar eventually made it to Abu Dhabi's Al Dhafra Region in an attempt to finally set a new production car top speed record and smash through that infamous 500 kph (310 mph) barrier.
And smash through it they did, with the YANGWANG U9 Xtreme topping out at 503.17 kph (312.65 mph), surpassing last year's record of 496.22 kph (308.33 mph). In doing so, it secured a total of four Guinness World Records for itself, as well as its tires. The U9 Xtreme is now the fastest production car in the world and the fastest electric production car in the world, while its Giti tires are the fastest EV tires in the world and fastest road car tires in the world.
This 500 kph threshold has been pursued by the automotive industry for a while now, with carmakers never quite being able to get there, especially by using conventional internal combustion powertrains. The fact that the U9 Xtreme is putting down a whopping 3,019 ps (2,978 hp) certainly helps.
"I always tell people that our engineers are young, bold and maybe a little crazy – but in a good way! And again, we must congratulate them and the whole YANGWANG U9X team for an incredible next step and these astonishing records," said BYD executive VP, Stella Li.
"Even as the team celebrated the astonishing 496.22km/h (308.22mph) in Germany last year, they were looking through the data and discussing how to take U9X to its next level. 503.17km/h (312.65mph) is a fantastic achievement, and it moves the benchmark for pure electric power even further ahead of where others might dream."
The path to 500+ kph was a gradual uphill battle. The regular U9 hypercar set its first benchmark back in 2024 by reaching 309 kph (192 mph) at Wuhan Hannah airport in China, before flying to Germany at the ATP Papenburg proving ground in order to lay down a 391.94 kph (243 mph) run - the same facility where the U9 Xtreme made its first appearance at, going directly to 472.41 kph (293.54 mph), before setting a new world production car speed record by hitting 496.22 kph (308.33 mph).
Photo: BYD Before this latest record run, YANGWANG engineers made some adjustments to the U9 Xtreme's rear-wing angle in order to increase rear-axle downforce, while also updating the suspension software to increase rebound damping and fine-tuning the tire pressures.
Naturally, the biggest upgrade was the EV powertrain in the U9X to begin with. It's got so much more power than the standard U9, it's almost laughable. Like they're two different cars. We're talking more than double the power, which is a staggering leap.
So, where do we go from here? Well, somebody will just have to come along and break this 503.17 kph record, and I doubt it's going to be Bugatti with the Tourbillon , since the latter "only" produces around 1,800 hp. But it's certainly not impossible. Also, the Koenigsegg Jesko Absolut might eventually have a say in this as well. On paper, it could do 500+ kph.

2026 SEMA Show • This Batmobile-Looking Lamborghini Temerario Is on Display at SEMA
Olympia Collection by Mulliner Honors the Lasting Legacy of W.O. Bentley With 12 Continental GTs
9 photos
Photo: Bentley Motors
The Olympia Collection by Mulliner consists of an exclusive collective of 12 individually numbered Bentley Continental GT coupes, making an ark across time to the unveiling of the legendary Bentley 6 ½ Liter, shown a century ago at the Olympia Motor Show 1926 in Britain.
Bentley is still focused on the new Torcal , as they follow up on the premiere with the development story behind the work done to bring it to life, but the company is also carefully taking care of other things, including its lasting legacy. Just recently, Bentley’s famous 4½ Liter Supercharged Team Car No. 2 (aka ‘Blower’) met the new Heritage Collection Blower Jnr by Hedley Studios and also the newly released 1:18 and 1:8 Amalgam Collection Blowers.
But now it’s time to spring back into full-size grand tourer action with the Olympia Collection: an exclusive Mulliner gathering “inspired by the journey, unveiling and legacy” of the legend car, but also the “engineering excellence and W.O. Bentley’s relentless spirit.” The ark across time is made with the 1926 Olympia Motor Show, where Bentley Motors revealed the production version of its second-ever model line, the six-cylinder 6 ½ Liter Bentley.
It was soon offered alongside the 3 Liter, with the new model aiming to broaden the appeal of the luxurious Bentley marque, “not just offering exceptional performance, but also effortless refinement.” 100 years later, the brand has prepared a collection of 12 Continental GTs to continue the story, “combining exhilarating performance with hand-crafted luxury.”
The new collection has a bespoke Verdant to Midnight Emerald Ombré exterior paint finish, created exclusively for this collection by Mulliner, and it’s matched with Champagne Gold badges and a lower bodywork pinstripe, set specifically as a recollection of the “golden hue of the nickel silver used for the radiator shells and switchgear of those early models.” There’s also a Blackline specification which darkens all the exterior brightwork, plus black 22-inch Mulliner wheels with face accents in Champagne Gold.
Last but not least, the outside of the cars has subtle Olympia Collection badges on the front wings, and when the doors open, an animated projection of a W.O. Bentley Lyon-Dieppe “spirited drive” meets the owner. Inside, the Olympia Collection has another exclusive color split: Cumbrian Green is the secondary hide while a bespoke Coach Green main hide has a heritage-patinated finish.
There are also black stained fascia and waistrails, open pore crown cut walnut veneer, while the controls and dials are now dressed in diamond knurling. The Bentley Rotating Display has special design details on the clock, an individual number, and the dials plus bezels directly recall the dials of the 1926 6 ½ Liter. Champagne Gold now features on the seat piping, gear lever, and organ stops. The box stitching on the steering wheel is in the same hue, aimed at mirroring the “look of the 1920s rope-bound steering wheels.”
The rear has unique ski hatch embroidery paying tribute to W.O. Bentley’s Lyon to Dieppe journey in a prototype six-cylinder Bentley, which then led to the development of the 6 ½ Liter, and Cumbrian Green embroidery is used to outline the region while the route is done in Champagne Gold.
The finishing touches are on the treadplates, done in black and with an ‘Olympia Collection by Mulliner’ motif, and all 12 examples of the Olympia Collection Continental GT models will get unique covers in green with Champagne Gold accents, along with a Brooklands watch, a commemorative handover box, and the story of the Olympia Collection book.

2026 SEMA Show • SRT Performance Joins the 2026 SEMA Show Featuring the First-Ever Jeep Wrangler Scrambler Concept
HayesX-250 Is the Newest American Personal eVTOL, Born in Las Vegas
9 photos
Photo: HayesX/Instagram
If you have been dreaming of an US-built personal eVTOL (electric vertical takeoff and landing) that allows you to fly without a pilot license and that can be delivered to you relatively fast, now is your chance – the brand-new HayesX-250 checks all of these boxes and is available for order, with a limited number of deliveries as soon as this year.
There are different types of electric aircraft marketed as personal eVTOLs, but a very limited number of those fall under the FAA (Federal Aviation Administration) Part 103 regulations – meaning single-seat vehicles under 254 lbs (empty) and with a maximum speed of 63 mph.
The most popular in this category worldwide is, no doubt, the Jetson One, originally developed in Europe. Another personal eVTOL in this category is the Chinese CoolFly Dream , introduced to the US market earlier this year, when it was on display at EAA AirVenture Oshkosh. Now, the newest name to join the ranks of this very exclusive club is HayesX, with its flagship aircraft, the HayesX-250.
You’ll notice that all three have very similar designs, centered around the single-seat configuration and an ultra-compact, but extremely protective shell. Their specifications are also very similar, since they all fall in line with the required FAA Part 103 requirements for maximum weight, speed, and so on.
The HayesX-250, which is making its official debut at this year’s SEMA Show at the Las Vegas Convention Center (4-6 November, 2026), is also priced almost the same as the ultra-popular Jetson One. The HayesX-250 can be ordered for $146,600, with a $6,000 deposit, while the Jetson One is priced at $148,000, with an $8,000 deposit.
The huge difference right now is in how fast you can get your hands on this personal eVTOL. The Las Vegas-based company is currently accepting a limited number of orders for 2026 delivery, which is incredibly fast, while the Jetson One production is already sold out for 2026 and 2027, with earliest deliveries available only in 2028.
In addition to an aviation-grade aluminum chassis, and an eight-electric motor configuration, this personal eVTOL comes with two big advantages. One is the multi-layered system redundancy and safety features, including a whole-aircraft ballistic parachute, with a clearance as low as ten meters (32.8 feet). The other is an ultra-compact design with folding arms, that allows easy transportation of the aircraft in a pickup or trailer.
What makes the HayesX-250 extra appealing is its versatility in terms of potential applications. Although technically a personal eVTOL, this single-seat vehicle isn’t meant just for leisure flights.
It can become an awesome work buddy for folks working in farm management, land development, and even search-and-rescue. From advanced aerial photography to emergency first aid, this lightweight, compact aircraft can prove to be highly useful, not just fun.

2026 SEMA Show • Ringbrothers Mesmerizes the SEMA Show Once Again, This Time With Billie, the 650-HP Pontiac GTO
Most Powerful Harley-Davidson Road Glide Gets Even Meaner for the 2027 Bagger World Cup
19 photos
Photo: Harley-Davidson
Here we are, at the end of the first-ever season of Harley-Davidson's first international one-make racing series. It proved to be a very successful one, it seems, with the bike maker claiming a combined attendance for the season of some 800,000 people, witnessing, over the course of six rounds, five different race winners, podium finishes for each participating team, and a fight for the title between four riders that extended into the final round.
It was only natural, thus, that the company would continue this event. In fact, it even announced it is exiting King of the Baggers , the U.S.-only racing series for baggers, to focus on this new project. Confirmation of a second season of the Bagger World Cup came this week during the EICMA show in Milan, Italy, and brought with it news of an expanded calendar, more teams, and, most importantly, a revised racing motorcycle.
The Bagger World Cup only allows trace-prepped Road Glides to line up on the starting grid, and that is what will happen during the 2027 season as well. Using lessons learned in the races this year, and input from the riders, the already insane beast became even meaner.
Photo: Harley-Davidson As presented last year, the DynoJet-prepped racer was fitted with a 131ci Screamin’ Eagle Milwaukee-Eight 131R V-twin engine whose racing ECU and dedicated mapping allowed it to develop over 200 horsepower and over 220 Nm of torque, enough for it to get to a top speed of 191 mph (300 kph) pretty fast.
That doesn't seem enough for the upcoming season, so Harley announced some changes that could make all the difference in the upcoming races. The upgrades target engine performance, the transmission, suspension, electronics, and durability.
When it comes to the Milwaukee-Eight, Harley speaks of the new Road Glides gaining up to three percent more power, and an increase in the rev limit from 7,000 to 7,200 rpm. The transmission the engine is tied to, on the other hand, gets a new Dynojet quickshifter sensor.
On the suspension front, Harley went for new fork caps that should allow for an increased ride height at the front, imagined independently adjustable damping settings for the rear shocks, and improved the swingarm to help the rear wheel with grip.
Photo: Harley-Davidson The other major change made to the racer includes the fitting of an active tire pressure monitoring system, but three more are on the way: updates to the bodywork and improved rider ergonomics with changes to the handlebar controls, foot positions and seating configurations.
Because all teams in this competition race the same bikes, all the changes mentioned above will be made available to all participating teams. Speaking of which, we know at the time of writing there will be five of them fielding 11 motorcycles, but more are likely to join the party before the second season kicks off.
Confirmed, for now, are teams Joe Rascal (which will line up three motorcycles), Saddlemen Race Development (also three motorcycles), Niti Racing (three bikes), Kyle Wyman Racing (one bike), and Mad Monkey / Tobacco Road Harley-Davidson (one bike). As a reminder, this season's winner was Joe Rascal's Archie McDonald.
Now officially titled the FIM Harley-Davidson Bagger World Cup Tuned by Dynojet, the competition will continue to be held in conjunction with MotoGP weekends, with each outing consisting of two full-points races, one qualifying session and two free practice sessions. That means we'll get a total of eight circuits and double the number of races.
Photo: Harley-Davidson Below you can have a look at the venues and the dates where the Road Glides will make a spectacle next year:
Round 1 | April 23–25 – MotoGP Grand Prix of the United States, COTA Round 2 | May 14–16 – MotoGP Grand Prix of France, Le Mans Round 3 | May 28–30 – MotoGP Grand Prix of Italy, Mugello Round 4 | June 11–13 – MotoGP Grand Prix of Catalonia, Barcelona Round 5 | June 25–27 – MotoGP Grand Prix of the Netherlands, Assen Round 6 | August 27–29 – MotoGP Grand Prix of Austria, Red Bull Ring Round 7 | September 17–19 – MotoGP Grand Prix of Aragón, MotorLand Aragón Round 8 | October 1–3 – MotoGP Grand Prix of Portugal, Portimão
Harley expects the crowd of people who will be in the stands for all of these races to grow by some 60 percent, reaching 1.3 million. That's probably owed to the three new destinations that have joined the calendar for next year, the ones in France, Spain , and Portugal.
Although the start of the second season of the Bagger World Cup is still some six months away, Harley is already selling early bird tickets for the COTA race, offering a 3-Day Harley-Davidson Bagger World Cup Fan Experience Pass for $149. The offer is limited, but the bike maker does not mention when it will expire - we'll keep an eye on things and report back once we know more.

source_document.body:
2026 SEMA Show • 2028 Mitsubishi Outlander Diamond Trail Edition: How Does It Compare to Other Adventure Crossovers?
SSR Performance's Project Leo Is a Twin-Turbo 911 GT3 RS With 911 GT2 RS Manthey Ambitions
14 photos
Photo: SH Proshots
One of the most exciting 911 specials yet, the 991 GT2 RS will soon gain an indirect successor based on the 992 GT3 RS. Enter the incredibly purposeful SSR Performance Project Leo, which is edging closer to production reality at the Green Hell. Just like Porsche's flagship 991, this fellow is an extreme interpretation of what the Neunelfer is supposed to be.
A simple glance at its rear quarter windows reveals that Munich-based SSR Performance had to rethink how the air moves into the engine compartment after giving the high-revving H6 a couple of snails. Large openings around the rear wheel arches can be seen as well, indicating very different cooling requirements from the naturally aspirated GT3 RS.
New vents are featured on top of the front fenders, and the front bumper wears double canards for improved aerodynamic stability. The aero-centric theme continues with a much larger front splitter, new skirts with altered intakes behind the doors, and the new diffuser out back.
Speaking of the rear end, the ginormous wing isn't the most dramatic element. Quad exhaust outlets that are facing the ground rather than the spy photographer suggest forced induction, and those four pipes make the rear end visually distinct from the dual center setup of the donor vehicle.
Back in April 2026, the German tuner and racing outfit published a teaser in which it described a proprietary high-performance cooling system for Project Leo. The rear side and bumper apertures are certainly part of the cooling-related changes, though it's too early to figure out the airflow target or the radiator layout.
Photo: SH Proshots Nevertheless, it sure is crazy to see how a turbo conversion of the GT3 RS has resulted in a comprehensive redesign of so many exterior panels and parts. The question is, how much power should we look forward to from Project Leo?
Porsche 's international website lists 525 ps and a top speed of 296 kph for the current GT3 RS, meaning 518 hp and 184 mph in American speak. Twin snails would result in 800 ponies at the very least, and with a bit of luck, Project Leo may be capable of exceeding 300 clicks on the Nurburgring's Dottinger Hohe.
As a brief refresher, the 991-generation GT2 RS offered 700 ps (690 hp) at full chatter and track speeds of up to 340 kph (211 mph). Regarding the current-gen GT3 RS, the biggest challenge to exceeding 300 clicks isn't power or gearing. It's aerodynamic drag, and SSR Performance needs to get it right if the company intends to smash the 911 GT2 RS Manthey's lap time at the Green Hell.
Speaking of Manthey, those disc-like wheels appear to be designed with aerodynamic efficiency and cooling in mind. A bespoke transmission application was confirmed by SSR, though it's not clear whether the company is developing on the PDK or uses a motorsport-infused sequential unit.
Expected to lap the Ring in less than 7 minutes, Project Leo has to prove itself against the 991 GT2 RS Manthey. It will be tremendously difficult, though. The Manthey-prepped 911 GT2 RS from the 991 generation blitzed the German circuit in 6:43.3 in 2021, whereas the Mercedes-AMG ONE hypercar required 6:29.090 to complete the full 20.8-kilometer lap.

2026 SEMA Show • 2027 Toyota Crown Signia Gets GT-S Concept Treatment for SEMA, Becomes a Sleek Wagon
Electra Closer to Ultra Short Aircraft Operations in New York City
8 photos
Photo: Electra
Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) isn’t limited to eVTOLs (electric vertical takeoff and landing). Electra’s EL9 Ultra Short combines hybrid-electric propulsion with an innovative take on fixed-wing design. The EL9 is like a greener regional aircraft boasting amazing versatility in terms of infrastructure, which translates to greater access and better efficiency, and all of these qualities could be soon experienced first-hand by folks in New York City.
Air travel from New York City to multiple communities across the region could become much faster, greener, and overall more efficient. A new partnership between Electra, the company behind the EL9 Ultra Short aircraft, and VertiPorts by Atlantic is already looking into the best infrastructure opportunities to support regular Ultra Short operations in the area.
As its name implies, the EL9 Ultra Short’s greatest advantage is the ability to take off and land within just 150 feet (45.7 meters). This means helicopter-like access for a fixed-wing aircraft that doesn’t have vertical takeoff and landing capabilities. Also, with a nine-passenger configuration and hybrid-electric propulsion that supports an extended range, EL9 checks the boxes of an efficient regional aircraft.
This innovative design is at the heart of Electra’s “Direct Aviation” concept, defined as a “new model of point-to-point regional travel.” It doesn’t require dedicated infrastructure built from scratch, just distributed access points added to an existing network, in key locations.
Electra ’s collaboration with this new infrastructure partner will focus specifically on new and existing VertiPorts by Atlantic sites in New York City, and how various types of infrastructure, such as barges and piers, could be integrated at these sites for Ultra Short operations.
VertiPorts by Atlantic is the vertiport subsidiary of Atlantic Aviation, an established operator with a large network of fixed base operations (FBOs) at more than 100 locations across North America. Through this subsidiary, Atlantic Aviation is expanding its expertise and actual network to develop and operate vertiport infrastructure in support of AAM.
Direct Aviation is ultimately about making regular connections between city hubs faster and more efficient. Electra’s recently-issued Direct Aviation Market Outlook estimates, among other things, that approximately one million passengers per day could benefit from this type of air mobility service within the first decade of operations. However, that requires a sufficient number of aircraft (from 12,000 to 16,000) and a solid network of distributed access points.
Electra has what it takes to make this happen, in cooperation with industry partners and with the support of an adequate regulatory framework. Earlier this year, it was named the Premier Private Participant in the eIPP (eVTOL Integration Pilot Program), America’s historic Advanced Air Mobility initiative.
Electra’s recent demonstration at Downtown Skyport in Lower Manhattan was most likely the first time a fixed-wing aircraft without vertical capabilities landed at the heliport.
Electra’s flagship, the EL9 Ultra Short, is currently aiming for full Type Certification with FAA (the Federal Aviation Administration). First flights are set to begin in late 2027 or early 2028.

2027 Toyota RAV4 Woodland Receives New Suspension Lift, PHEVs Get the NACS Port and More Potent AC
66 photos
Photo: Toyota Motor Corporation
The 2027 Toyota RAV4 comes with enhancements, but unfortunately, they're not available on every model; the Woodland and PHEVs get all the attention. One major detail isn’t missing: MSRPs.
The Toyota Motor Corporation (TMC), the world’s largest and most valuable automaker, just announced its financial results for the second quarter, which ended September 30, 2026, and it almost got a positive result: consolidated global vehicle deliveries were 4.758 million units, missing the mark by just 25k vehicles compared to last year.
In North America, they were even closer to a positive quarter: 1.53 million units, and the slide was just 3k examples. However, the region’s operating income without interest rate swaps increased by 266.1 billion yen ($1.67 billion). As for Toyota Motor North America, or TMNA , its local division, the company is very busy focusing on the 2027 model year changeover, especially for the namesake Toyota brand.
We have recently seen the details regarding the 2027 Toyota Tundra, which gains a refreshed exterior, an upgraded TRD Pro suspension, “significant enhancements” in towing technology, and, most importantly, access to the new Trailhunter package. But Toyota also announced the 2027 Sequoia, Crown Signia, Camry, Corolla Cross, Grand Highlander with the new Woodland Edition, or the trio of electrics previously.
Well, now it’s time for the main attraction: Toyota’s regular best-seller is still trying to catch up to its previous generation, and so far, this year it has conceded the throne of the compact crossover SUV class to the Honda CR-V, but the RAV4 is not giving up the crown without a fight. So, the 2027 RAV4 “remains Toyota’s benchmark small SUV, offering a fully electrified lineup in a choice of HEV and PHEV powertrains, available FWD or AWD, and a broad range of grades tailored to different driving lifestyles.”
The second model year of the sixth generation comes with “two notable updates for the new model year: a revised suspension for the RAV4 Woodland grade, pushing ground clearance up to 9.1 inches, and the addition of a NACS port for all PHEV grades.” The 2027 Toyota RAV4 Woodland is arguably the bigger news: the off-road-focused grade receives new suspension components, including new springs, shocks, and jounce bumpers, raising the ground clearance from 8.1 inches on all the other trim levels except the GR Sport, which has it even lower to a new standard of 9.1 inches.
The Woodland also gains redesigned all-weather floor and cargo mats, while all PHEV models now have a NACS port and DC fast charging (Level 3) capability, with the charging port now situated on the driver’s side on all PHEVs, and the new onboard AC charger has a speed of 11 kW on all PHEV grades. Additionally, all trim levels gain a backup camera washer, while the AWD models now have Multi-Terrain Select with Rock & Dirt and Mud & Sand modes.
The Multi-Terrain Select replaces Trail mode and Snow mode can be accessed now via the drive mode select switch alongside Normal, Eco, Sport, and Custom, plus the Remote Connect trial has been increased from one to no less than five years for all grades. MSRPs kick off at $32,300 for the LE FWD grade – as opposed to $31,900 for the 2026 model year. The PHEVs now kick off at $42,100 for the SE, which was $41,500 before. So, what do you think – yay or nay?

Think Android Auto Is Buggy? Just Wait for Gemini. New Phone Call Headache Unlocked
6 photos
Photo: Google
Surprised about the headline? Don’t be. Gemini certainly isn’t the flawless assistant that so many people have been waiting for, and a new glitch that’s now plaguing Samsung Galaxy and Google Pixel phones is living proof.
It’s no secret that Gemini doesn’t like to make phone calls, but this new behavior pushes the frustration level to a new high.
It’s because Gemini seemingly understands what users say but keeps repeating the same question over and over again. “Who do you want to call?” Gemini says, even when clearly being told the name of the contact.
Users explain that, initially, the conversation with Gemini works correctly. Waking the digital assistant and prompting it to initiate seemingly works correctly, too, until one point when the name of the contact is being spoken.
“Who do you want to call?” Gemini asks. Jessica. Tom. Jim. Alex. Monica. No matter the name, Gemini keeps asking the same question.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Users who got angry with this problem started looking into it on their own and discovered that the problem somehow resides between the moment a phone call is supposed to be initiated and the one when Gemini needs to pick a contact for the phone call. In other words, Gemini can make phone calls correctly, only that it can’t process the contact’s name.
The ability to make phone calls is also working correctly when Gemini must dial a phone number. If you remember a contact’s phone number, telling Gemini to dial it, digit by digit, works correctly. Tell the assistant the contact’s name, and it’s stuck in the same loop.
It looks like Gemini doesn’t make a difference between phone models, so pretty much any Samsung and Pixel devices are affected. The latest-generation models are also experiencing the same problems, so even if you bought a Samsung Galaxy S26, you’ll end up battling the same bugs in your car.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Users who turned to Google’s Community forums to report the glitch claim they’ve tried any other workaround they could think of, including the typical fixes that involve clearing the app’s cache and removing the updates. Nothing worked, and more frustratingly, users end up struggling with all of these when they run Android Auto - a Google app - on a Google phone - the Google Pixel.
“I'm using a Pixel 10, latest updates, in a 2021 VW GTI. This is a Google phone that won't work with a Google app! I'm stuck with Gemini, and it even corrects the spelling of the name of the person I'm trying to message or call on the screen, so it knows who I'm trying to reach! I swear this app works one month out of the year correctly, and the rest of the time it is super buggy. So frustrating,” someone posted on the forums.
A Google Community specialist is asking for additional information about the glitch, so theoretically, an investigation should already be underway. It’s too early to tell when a patch could land, but considering how many people are complaining about similar problems, it’d better go live as soon as possible.
The glitch first appeared in October , and considering going back to Google Assistant is no longer an option after Google enforced the transition to Gemini and killed off the old assistant, users are left with no solution but to wait for a patch.
“I have tried to update Android Auto in the Play Store, but it only gives me the option to uninstall. I have uninstalled and reinstalled with no help. I have also cleared the cache, but I am still unable to call or text to known contacts. It will allow me to call or text when I state the phone number, but that requires that I know the phone number. I have also tried to find a way to update my contacts in Android Auto or on my phone, but that is not an option that I can find,” someone explains .
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution This isn’t the first time Gemini has caused headaches on Android Auto, as the experience with the new AI-powered assistant has been unpolished, to say the least.
Users have previously complained of another phone call bug that prevented them from making phone calls , but others claimed that Gemini couldn’t even call 911 in case of emergency. Others explained that Gemini caused app crashes in the middle of the drive.
With a patch still in the works, the only thing you can do right now is to keep all apps up-to-date by enabling automatic updates on the Google Play Store. Google has recently shipped Android Auto 18.1, and the rollout should gain more traction in the coming weeks, though it doesn’t look like this new version includes a patch. You should also keep the Google app up to date, as this is the one responsible for the experience with Gemini on Android devices and Android Auto.
